title: Bayesian Low-Rank Posteriors for Scalable Membership Inference
topic: Social Aspects->Privacy-preserving Statistics and Machine Learning
claim: Replace costly ensembles of reference models by sampling cheap virtual references from a posterior fitted in one training run.
layout: 2 stacked bands, 4 numbered stages left-to-right, contour plots and distributions
description: The figure has two stacked, color-banded panels. The top maroon band, "Bayesian Reference Approximation", starts at the left with a shadow model: a document image and question feed a frozen pre-trained VLM plus a trainable LoRA block, with a shadow-dataset icon below. Step 1 is a loss-landscape contour plot with an SGD trajectory and yellow snapshot dots. Step 2 is a 2D Gaussian posterior with elliptical contours, and the SWAG Gaussian formula sits above it. The bottom blue band, "Target-conditioned Membership Inference", shows step 3: K sampled adapters feeding Reference Model (1) through (K) in a dashed box. Step 4 sends the target document and question into a locked Target Model and a Reference Ensembles box. Two null-distribution curves follow, one brown (IN) and one green (OUT), each with a p=0.05 threshold. Numbered circles guide the reading order, and big hollow arrows link the stages.
caption: Overview of LIBRA. (1) LoRA fine-tuning on shadow data; snapshots collected along the SGD trajectory. (2) SWAG fits a Gaussian posterior over the LoRA subspace from these snapshots (contours show a 2D projection). (3) K adapters sampled from the posterior yield virtual reference models sharing frozen backbone. (4) Reference scores form an empirical null p(S | H0); a one-sided test rejects non-membership when the target deviates from the null (direction depends on S).
abstract: Membership inference attacks (MIAs) aim to determine whether a sample was used during the training of a target model. Strong MIAs rely on reference (or shadow) models to estimate target-conditional score distributions, but training such ensembles is computationally expensive for modern large-scale Vision--Language Models (VLMs). In this work, we propose a scalable alternative that replaces explicit reference-model training with a Bayesian approximation over low-rank adaptation parameters. Specifically, we model uncertainty only within the LoRA subspace and construct a posterior from a single training run, from which we sample a diverse set of \emph{virtual reference models}. We instantiate this approach using Stochastic Weight Averaging Gaussian (SWAG), enabling efficient approximation of target-conditional score distributions at a fraction of the cost of conventional shadow-model ensembles. We evaluate the resulting attack on three downstream-adapted VLMs across two privacy-sensitive visual question answering tasks, namely Document VQA and Medical VQA. To isolate the effect of pretraining knowledge, we additionally introduce a controlled synthetic dataset. Our approach outperforms standard reference-based attacks while requiring only a single reference-model fine-tuning run, making membership inference more practical for large VLMs.
